correctness.rationale: Starting from the primary source's explicit \(u,v,y,Z\), \(y\) simplifies to a nonnegative affine function of \(\cosh(2|B|/T)\), so concurrence positivity is equivalent to the sign of \(y^2-uv\). Independent expansion reconstructs exactly the stated quadratic coefficients. The leading coefficient is positive exactly when \(\sinh^2x>\cosh(\sqrt2 x)\); its difference is strictly increasing for \(x>0\), giving a unique root. Above the corresponding temperature the quadratic is negative for every admissible field; below it, opposite-sign roots and negativity at zero field yield exactly one positive threshold. Standard asymptotic expansion of those exact coefficients gives the stated low-temperature activation law and high-field positive tail. The numerical root \(x_*=1.4195389207530749\ldots\) and \(T_*/|J|=0.7044540909589808\ldots\) were independently reproduced.
